# Discover competitors

Record name, canonical URL, aliases, audience, use cases and geography with evidence. Use repository manifests and public documentation if no URL is supplied. Mark uncertain inferences and ask when different identities would change the panel.

Search the relevant category, a concrete buyer use case and alternatives. Save exact queries, timestamps, returned links and pages actually fetched as separate evidence. Cite product/documentation pages for features. Record inaccessible sources and failed tool outcomes; use another source or leave the claim unresolved.

Each competitor needs a stable id, name, URL, `direct` or `adjacent` relationship, reason and evidence ids. Direct competitors solve substantially the same job for the same audience. Adjacent products cover part of the job or another audience. Directory mentions are not market share. Present the list as correctable.

Discovery has brand context and never counts as independent measurement. Corrections create a new panel revision with the earlier snapshot retained.
